title: Muzaffarids
capsule: The Muzaffarid dynasty was an Iranian Muslim ruling house founded by Mubariz al-Din Muhammad, who rose to power in Fars and Kirman after the Ilkhanate's dissolution, capturing Shiraz in 1353. Shah Shuja (r. 1358–1384) was the dynasty's most capable ruler, patronizing the poet Hafez at his Shiraz court and temporarily resisting Timurid pressure. The dynasty was extinguished in 1393–94 when Timur (Tamerlane), having taken Isfahan in 1387 and Shiraz in 1393, executed the last Muzaffarid princes and annexed their territories into his empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Muzaffarid territories in Fars, Kirman, and Isfahan are well documented in Persian chronicle sources; exact boundaries fluctuated significantly through dynastic internecine conflict in the 1360s–1390s.
